effects: The signer sends `assets` WETH to the vault (safeTransferFrom(_asset, caller, this, assets)).
The vault mints bbETH shares to `receiver`; the share count comes from the stored share price, rounded down, and has no minimum bound.
The vault supplies the WETH to Morpho Blue markets; this moves the vault's funds, not the signer's.
Fee shares can be minted to the fee recipient before the price is computed; this is already part of the share price.
formats.shown: Intent 'Deposit', with the WETH amount, a constant 'Share ticker: bbETH' and the share recipient; the number of shares is not shown.

findings.title: deposit does not show how many bbETH shares the receiver gets; the share price comes from storage.
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.deposit: `shares = _convertToSharesWithTotals(assets, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Floor);` Descriptor shows only 'Share ticker' raw `$.metadata.constants.vaultTicker`. Case 0: signer receives 0.05 bbETH, and the screen gives no amount.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show it. Optionally rename the label to 'Receive bbETH shares' and drop the separate ticker field.

findings.title: deposit intent 'Deposit' does not name the asset or say that vault shares come back.
findings.evidence: descriptor deposit: "intent": "Deposit"; the field label 'Deposit asset' holds an amount, not an asset.
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Deposit WETH for bbETH shares" and the label to "Amount".

cases.notes: WETH 0.05 out is shown correctly. bbETH 0.05 in: the ticker and receiver are shown, the amount is not (storage-derived).

effects: The signer sends WETH to the vault; the amount is convertToAssets(shares), rounded up from the stored share price, with no maximum other than the signer's allowance.
The vault mints exactly `shares` bbETH to `receiver`.
The vault supplies the WETH to Morpho Blue; this moves the vault's funds only.
formats.shown: Intent 'Mint', 'Deposit asset: WETH' with no amount, the share amount in bbETH and the share recipient.

findings.title: mint does not show how much WETH leaves the signer; the amount comes from the stored share price.
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.mint: `assets = _convertToAssetsWithTotals(shares, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Ceil);` then `_deposit(_msgSender(), receiver, assets, shares)`. Descriptor field 'Deposit asset' is raw `$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker` only.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds the amount. Label the field 'Pay with (amount set by share price)' so the signer knows the amount is not fixed.

findings.title: mint intent 'Mint' does not say that the signer pays WETH for the shares.
findings.evidence: descriptor mint: "intent": "Mint"; ERC4626._deposit: `SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom(_asset, caller, address(this), assets);`
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Deposit WETH to mint bbETH shares".

findings.title: mint test case uses a reverted transaction to 0x…01, so it shows no real mint.
findings.fix: Add a test case from a successful mint to a real receiver.

cases.notes: The mined transaction reverted (status 0), so it has no effects. Judged from the code only.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)
effects: The vault burns bbETH shares from `owner`; the count is convertToShares(assets), rounded up from the stored share price.
If the signer is not `owner`, the vault spends that many shares of the owner's allowance to the signer.
The vault sends exactly `assets` WETH to `receiver`.
formats.shown: Intent 'Withdraw', 'Withdraw exactly' in WETH, the recipient 'To' and 'Owner'; the shares burned are not mentioned.

findings.title: withdraw does not show how many bbETH shares it burns from the owner; the count comes from storage.
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.withdraw: `shares = _convertToSharesWithTotals(assets, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Ceil);` ERC4626._withdraw: `_burn(owner, shares);`. Case 2: signer loses 0.0125 bbETH, and no field mentions shares.
findings.fix: No calldata value holds the count. Rename 'Owner' to 'Burn bbETH shares from' so the burn is stated.

findings.title: withdraw label 'Owner' does not say that this account's bbETH shares are burned.
findings.evidence: descriptor withdraw field `owner` label "Owner"; ERC4626._withdraw: `_spendAllowance(owner, caller, shares); _burn(owner, shares);`. Case 2 reader: 'share tokens may be burned (screen doesn't say)'.
findings.fix: Change the label to "Burn bbETH shares from" and the intent to "Withdraw WETH by burning bbETH".

cases.notes: WETH 0.0125 in to the signer is shown right. The 0.0125 bbETH burn has no field, so the reader only guessed it.

formats.key: redeem(uint256 shares, address receiver, address owner)
effects: The vault burns exactly `shares` bbETH from `owner`, spending the owner's allowance to the signer when they differ.
The vault sends WETH to `receiver`; the amount is convertToAssets(shares), rounded down from the stored share price, with no minimum.
formats.shown: Intent 'Redeem', the shares to redeem in bbETH, 'To' and 'Owner'; nothing names WETH or the amount received.

findings.title: redeem never names WETH as the asset the receiver gets back.
findings.evidence: ERC4626._withdraw: `SafeERC20.safeTransfer(_asset, receiver, assets);` The redeem fields are only shares, To and Owner; mint has a constant `underlyingTicker` field, redeem has none. Case 3: signer receives 5.429881960509717696 WETH; reader: 'likely ETH/WETH, amount not shown'.
findings.fix: Add {"label": "Receive asset", "format": "raw", "value": "$.metadata.constants.underlyingTicker"} and change the intent to "Redeem bbETH for WETH".

findings.title: redeem does not show the WETH amount received; it comes from the stored share price with no minimum.
findings.evidence: MetaMorpho.redeem: `assets = _convertToAssetsWithTotals(shares, totalSupply(), newTotalAssets, Math.Rounding.Floor);` and there is no minAssets parameter.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show the amount.

cases.notes: The 5.2459 bbETH burn is shown right, with the owner resolved through ENS. The 5.4299 WETH received has no asset or amount on screen.
